en: My love, who leaves me behind and goes,
will not go even ten ri before his feet fall sick.
In the clear blue sky there are many small stars,
and in our hearts there are many dreams.
That mountain over there, they say, is Baekdusan;
even in the eleventh and twelfth months, only flowers bloom.
notes: lines 1.1, 2.1, 3.1: 'arirang' and 'arariyo' are refrain words with no agreed meaning; kept untranslated. 'Arirang' in line 2 is the name of the pass (gogae, a hill pass), real or imagined.
line 1.2 (and 2.2, 3.2): the subject is unstated; 'one goes' (literally 'crosses over by Arirang Pass'). It can be read as the singer or the departing lover.
line 1.3: 'nim' is a respectful word for the beloved; the honorific verb 'gasineun' ('who goes', honorific) shows respect even in reproach. The beloved's sex is not stated; 'his' is a choice.
line 1.4: ten ri (sim-ri) is about 4 km, i.e. not far at all; 'balbyeong nanda' = 'gets foot sickness', sore or lame feet.
line 2.4: other sung versions have 'sorrows' or 'worries' (e.g. 수심) here instead of 'dreams' (꿈); the imported text has 꿈.
line 3.3: Baekdusan (Mount Paektu), the highest mountain of Korea, on the border with China; kept as a name.
line 3.4: 'dongji seotdal' = the month of the winter solstice (the 11th lunar month) and the last (12th) lunar month, i.e. the depth of winter.
rom: RR follows pronunciation, so 십리 is 'simni', 많고/많다 'manko'/'manta', 꽃만 'kkonman'; spacing as in the original (못가서 one word).
